## A study has been run against this problem

Fitting one shared interaction matrix on a globally centered covariate is not pooling: for a binary modifier with study prevalence p_s it is algebraically identical to imposing that the causal within-trial coefficient equals the confounded across-trial one. In the model simulated, coverage of a nominal 95% interval for the causal interaction falls from 93.8% when that happens to be true to 17.2% when the two are equal and opposite, and further in networks whose contrasts move two components at once. Separating them costs about 5% in interval width and removes an order of magnitude of bias. The catalog's stated cause is incomplete: the loss is present with all twelve trials supplying individual data, so aggregate data are not necessary for it, but removing individual data roughly doubles the bias, so they amplify it. [Read the study below](#our-study).
:::

## Statement

In mixed IPD and aggregate-data ML-NMR, interaction directions without adequate within-study IPD support may be weakly identified or nonidentified and are then sensitive to aggregate-study variation, shared-interaction restrictions and priors, and one coefficient forced to carry both within-study and between-study variation conflates individual-level effect modification with an ecological gradient. How far this bites is design- and parameter-specific rather than a categorical property of the method. The auditors disagreed on scope and the disagreement stands: the literature auditor found each claim confirmed almost verbatim by the ML-NMR authors, who report that the secukinumab interaction estimates rest solely on aggregate data and that the shared-interaction restriction was required to identify the model (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162), while the source-code auditor judged the diagnostic void overstated, because cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that cannot be installed from CRAN, already labels whether a row is identified by IPD, by between-study gradients or by neither, and flags posteriors that simply reproduce their priors.

## Why it is open

Studies contributing only aggregate data inform covariate effects mainly through between-study contrasts, so when the model imposes one coefficient for both sources an ecological gradient is read as individual-level modification and the fit still looks good. Flags help but do not identify: labeling a parameter as aggregate-informed or as prior-driven tells a reader where to distrust the estimate without supplying the missing within-study information. The remedy the source proposes, splitting interactions by treatment, is described by the ML-NMR authors as possible given sufficient data and an interesting avenue for further research, so it has not been evaluated, and the general-likelihood extension (doi:10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169) leaves the integration-distribution requirement intact.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Phillippo et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis, Medical Decision Making](https://doi.org/10.1177/0272989X221117162) | assesses population-adjustment assumptions inside a nine-study network: splits the common class interaction into treatment-specific interactions one covariate at a time, checks conditional constancy through residual heterogeneity and inconsistency in sufficiently large networks, and reports that the shared-interaction restriction was required to identify the model where a treatment was informed only by aggregate data |
| [Phillippo et al. 2025, Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods (arXiv:2401.12640), Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A](https://doi.org/10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169) | extends ML-NMR to general likelihoods; the specified integration distribution for aggregate-data studies remains a requirement of the method |
| [cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9, R/estimability.R and R/plot-mlnmr.R](https://github.com/choxos/cpaic) | estimable_effects_at() labels whether a component by effect-modifier row is identified by IPD, by between-study covariate gradients or by neither, and plot_prior_posterior() exposes parameters whose posteriors reproduce their priors; these flag the problem rather than solving it |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Do not rebuild the flags; make them standard and test them. Evaluate in simulation whether identified-by labeling, prior-to-posterior contraction and prior-data conflict checks actually detect the within-versus-between conflation when the truth is known, and report them next to estimates rather than on request. Fit within-study centered specifications that separate within-study from between-study coefficients, and treatment-specific interactions with hierarchical shrinkage, the avenue the ML-NMR authors flag as unexplored, then characterize how much IPD each interaction needs before its posterior stops tracking its prior.

## Our study

::: {.study-result}
**Separating within-trial from across-trial component effect modification**

*This study was designed against [CMP-13](https://github.com/choxos/ITC-open-problems/tree/main/studies/CMP-13-within-between-interaction) and bears on this entry in part. What it does not answer is stated below.*

**The question put to it.** Component ML-NMR fits one shared interaction on a globally centered covariate, which algebraically forces the causal within-trial interaction to equal the confounded across-trial association. How much does that cost, when, and is the damage really caused by aggregate data as the catalog claims?

**What it found.** Fitting one shared interaction matrix on a globally centered covariate is not pooling: for a binary modifier with study prevalence p_s it is algebraically identical to imposing that the causal within-trial coefficient equals the confounded across-trial one. In the model simulated, coverage of a nominal 95% interval for the causal interaction falls from 93.8% when that happens to be true to 17.2% when the two are equal and opposite, and further in networks whose contrasts move two components at once. Separating them costs about 5% in interval width and removes an order of magnitude of bias. The catalog's stated cause is incomplete: the loss is present with all twelve trials supplying individual data, so aggregate data are not necessary for it, but removing individual data roughly doubles the bias, so they amplify it.

**Results.**

- Coverage under the shared restriction degrades monotonically with the discordance between the within-trial and across-trial coefficients, from 93.8% at no discordance to 17.2% when they are equal and opposite, and it is worse in bundled component networks whose contrasts move two components at once than where every contrast isolates one.
- Both separated estimators are nominal at every discordance examined, 92.6% to 96.3%, including under a nonlinear across-trial pattern where the linear split model is itself misspecified.
- CMP-13 says aggregate studies cause the pull. With all twelve trials supplying individual patient data the shared model still has median absolute standardized bias 0.15 and coverage as low as 44.6%, so aggregate data are not necessary. But bias rises to 0.29 and coverage falls to 17.2% as individual data are removed, so they amplify it. The registered refutation threshold was narrowly missed (47% of cells against 50%) and we report that rather than moving it.
- Where a component appears in no individual-data arm, the three methods behave in three different ways: the IPD-anchored estimator declines to report it in 100% of replicates; the shared model returns a confident -0.34 against a truth of zero, sourced entirely from the across-trial gradient; and the joint split returns intervals so wide that coverage approaches one, when it returns one at all.
- A study-clustered sandwich, included so the comparison could not be won on the variance estimator, covered 75.4% to 92.4% where the shared model is correctly specified. With twelve clusters it is badly anticonservative, and it is reported as a finding rather than used as the comparator.

**Design.**

Estimand
:   Within-trial component interaction on the conditional log-rate scale

Methods compared
:   shared-info (status quo), shared-sandwich, joint-split, ipd-anchored

Data-generating mechanism
:   Twelve-trial two-component Poisson network with a binary effect modifier whose prevalence varies across studies, aggregate arms generated by exact integration. 320 scenarios crossing network structure, the discordance between within-trial and across-trial modification, IPD availability including a case where one component has no within-trial data at all, arm size and prevalence spread. 2000 replicates each.

Replicates
:   2000 per scenario, 640,000 networks

**What this does not answer.** The registered global analysis is uninformative and the regime split that produced a usable answer was prompted by observing that failure, so it is not prespecified. The general headline about component ML-NMR is not established: the likelihood and nuisance structures are not mapped onto the fixed- and random-effect specifications the implemented method offers, and free study-by-treatment effects or priors can absorb or alter the term the identity isolates. A maximum-likelihood analogue of component ML-NMR. Implemented ML-NMR is Bayesian and priors matter most where interactions are weakly identified, so the coverage numbers do not transfer to multinma; the algebra does, and therefore so does the direction. One binary modifier, a log link, a Poisson outcome, additive components with no synergy, no random treatment-effect heterogeneity, no inconsistency, and exactly reported study prevalences. Under the discordance patterns the split model is correctly specified, so the study measures the cost of an algebraically known restriction rather than establishing that real networks contain within/across disagreement or how large it typically is. Continuous or multiple correlated modifiers, misspecified aggregate covariate distributions, and time-to-event outcomes are untested. It does not touch IDN-05.

**Peer review.** 2 rounds, two independent reviewers. The reports, the point-by-point responses and the editorial decision are published in full: [read the review](/studies/CMP-13-within-between-interaction/out/CMP-13-peer-review.md).

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Partially addressed. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides. Reopened by the full-text reading: 5 findings from 5 papers survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from unverifiable to partially-addressed.

**The source titled this.** "ML-NMR interaction parameters are only partially identified" The title states partial identification as a categorical property of the method, which the audit found to be design- and parameter-specific.

**The source said.** "ML-NMR relies on conditional constancy of relative effects, a correct individual-level model, a specified integration distribution, and shared-interaction restrictions where needed. Partial identifiability of its interaction parameters and conflation of within-study with between-study effect modification remain unresolved weaknesses."

**What was wrong with it.** The source stated partial identifiability as a categorical weakness and said nothing in standard output separates a parameter learned from data from one supplied by the prior. The source-code auditor found identifiability parameter- and design-specific and found both flags already implemented in cpaic at commit 9d150e9, while the literature auditor found the claims confirmed by the ML-NMR authors themselves; the entry is published as unverifiable because both readings carry evidence, and it is now sourced to doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162, for which it previously cited nothing.

**Dissent.** codex dissented (overstated): C1 and C2 are technically sound: ML-NMR transports conditional relative-effect models and must integrate aggregate-study likelihood contributions over specified covariate distributions. C3 is too categorical. Interaction identifiability is parameter- and design-specific: interactions may be well identified by adequate within-trial IPD variation, weakly identified, or nonidentified. Aggregate arms can identify model-dependent integrated functionals and sometimes interaction combinations, rather than supplying only a generic ecological gradient. C4 is correct as a possibility when one coefficient is forced to represent both within-study and between-study variation. The report also overstates the diagnostic void for cpaic at 9d150e9: estimable_effects_at() labels whether information is from IPD, aggregate gradients, or neither, while plot_prior_posterior() exposes parameters whose posteriors reproduce their priors. These diagnostics flag rather than solve the underlying identification problem.

**Revised by the full-text reading.** Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed
:   **unverifiable -> partially-addressed** 5 surviving findings from: A framework for identifying treatment-covariate interactions; An overview of methods for network meta-analysis using indiv; Comparing the use of aggregate data and various methods of i; Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis: A Handbook for He; Network meta-analysis combining individual patient and aggre. New citations: 10.1002/jrsm.1300, 10.1177/0962280216660741, 10.1186/s12874-015-0007-0, 10.1186/s12874-021-01254-5

Literature and prior-art check
:   **open / supported.** This entry has no prior_work at all, yet every one of its four claims is confirmed almost verbatim by a paper by the ML-NMR authors themselves, which I read in full. On partial identifiability: in the psoriasis network the secukinumab interaction estimates 'are much more uncertain than for the ixekizumab regimens, as the secukinumab parameters are based solely on AgD, and the ixekizumab data largely drive the interaction estimates in the common interaction model', and the shared-interaction restriction was 'required to identify the model'. On within-versus-between conflation, Phillippo et al. state the ecological-bias mechanism explicitly and flag the entry's own proposed remedy as unexplored: 'it is possible to fit ML-NMR models where the interaction terms are split in this manner (given sufficient data), and this is an interesting avenue for further research.' That is a source asserting the gap, which is the strongest evidence a 'this is open' claim can have. The integration-distribution requirement is intrinsic to ML-NMR and restated in the general-likelihood extension (arXiv 2401.12640 / JRSS-A 10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169). I recommend the catalog attach Phillippo et al. 2023 as prior_work rather than publishing this entry unsourced.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** C1 and C2 are technically sound: ML-NMR transports conditional relative-effect models and must integrate aggregate-study likelihood contributions over specified covariate distributions. C3 is too categorical. Interaction identifiability is parameter- and design-specific: interactions may be well identified by adequate within-trial IPD variation, weakly identified, or nonidentified. Aggregate arms can identify model-dependent integrated functionals and sometimes interaction combinations, rather than supplying only a generic ecological gradient. C4 is correct as a possibility when one coefficient is forced to represent both within-study and between-study variation. The report also overstates the diagnostic void for cpaic at 9d150e9: estimable_effects_at() labels whether information is from IPD, aggregate gradients, or neither, while plot_prior_posterior() exposes parameters whose posteriors reproduce their priors. These diagnostics flag rather than solve the underlying identification problem.

Decision path
:   `R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present`

:::

## How the evidence falls in time

15 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2013 to 2024. Partial progress is on the record, and later work still calls this open. Both belong in view.

This problem is **recurrent**: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group's framing.

It is also being **closed in pieces**: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.
